title: skyBlip device status dump (v1)
description: ONE dump, TWO surfaces, one table behind both (firmware/core/comms/diagnostics.h). Over the companion link it is this object, requested with {"cmd":"diag"} on the config endpoint and answered as one frame per subsystem, or more where the negotiated ATT payload cannot carry a subsystem whole: every frame is a complete flat object carrying cmd, group, part and more, no frame mixes two groups, and no frame exceeds the payload the central negotiated (a notification over the payload is not truncated by the controller, it fails). Over USB CDC the same table is printed unsolicited every ten seconds as one line per subsystem, '<group> key=value key="text value" ...', with the same group names, the same keys and the same values - a laptop on the bench and a phone on the wing must not report a device differently. {"cmd":"radio"} asks for the radio group alone and answers under cmd 'radio'. Requesting the whole dump before the device has collected one is refused with {"ack":false,"reason":"no_stats"}: a device must not report health it has not measured. Nothing here is reset by being read, and no value is a settings change - this schema is read-only. The producer (firmware) owns it; consumers pin a version.

cmd.description: The question this frame answers. 'diag' is every group; 'radio' is the radio group alone

group.description: The subsystem every field in this frame belongs to. One console line per group, in this order

part.description: Frame index within one answer, from 0. A group that does not fit the negotiated payload spans consecutive parts

more.description: Another frame follows. Exactly one frame per answer carries false

up_s.description: sys. Seconds since boot, from hal::Clock::millis(). Wraps with the 32-bit millisecond counter at 49.7 days

reset.description: sys. Why the device came up, as core/power/reset_reason.cpp spells it: POWER ON, RESET PIN, BROWNOUT, SOFTWARE, WATCHDOG, CPU LOCKUP, CHARGER, WAKE, DEBUGGER, UNKNOWN

charger_woke.description: sys. Since the last boot that ran, a charger woke the unit out of SYSTEM OFF and that boot was refused: the cable reached the application. Kept through the rails in GPREGRET2, true for the one boot that follows and false from the boot after. The self-test page prints the same fact as USB WOKE (firmware/core/power/README.md)

link_drops.description: sys. Frames the companion link could not send: over the negotiated payload, refused by the controller, or left incomplete by a writer. Silence towards a phone is a fault worth a number

noise_dbm.description: radio. The measured noise floor, core/timing::NoiseFloor, in dBm. A diagnostic and nothing else: nothing on this device defers a burst to what it hears, so a loud site is reported rather than transmitted around (firmware/core/timing/README.md)

duty_permille.description: radio. Parts per thousand of the transmit allowance spent over the hour's sliding window (EN 300 220-2 V3.3.1 Table 4 band M, 1%). The declared channel-access route, and the only rule that refuses a burst

rx_bad.description: radio. Receptions that are a fault: a frame that framed, was attempted and was refused, plus the integrity failures an error correction could not rescue. Not a burst nothing was attempted on (rx_wait), not a message type this firmware does not implement (rx_type), not a burst that named no system at all (rx_unframed), not a frame keyed on a second we disagree with (rx_miskeyed), and not a transmission of ours that never completed (tx_lost)

rx_wait.description: radio. Frames no decode was attempted on, because an ALP-TAS position is coded relative to the receiver and keyed on the UTC second, so it needs a fix and a date of our own. Climbs on a device still acquiring next to a transmitting neighbour, which is correct behaviour and not a failure

rx_type.description: radio. Frames that framed and carried a message type this firmware does not implement: ALP-TAS reads its 2024 position frame and nothing else, so a SoftRF interleaving Air V6 with Air V7 lands here. The neighbour's dialect, not our failure

rx_unframed.description: radio. Bursts that held the shared sync window and decoded too cleanly to be noise, but whose sync tail named neither M-band system. A neighbour on another dialect, or a receiver framing at the wrong offset: either way not a frame this firmware refused

rx_miskeyed.description: radio. ALP-TAS frames whose CRC held and whose sender keyed them on a second inside 18 s of ours but not ours: the key stage moves every 16 s and the frame carries the low 4 bits of its own second, so a clock disagreement is reported as the offset it is rather than as a decode failure. Climbing here means one of the two clocks is wrong, not the radio

rx_noise.description: radio. What the band's own noise framed: a sync window that filled with something carrying no frame at all. The floor under every other reception counter, and the one that tells a deaf receiver from an empty sky

tx_ok.description: radio. Bursts the executor reported as transmitted

tx_keyed_us.description: radio. Microseconds the last burst held the carrier keyed, measured by the executor rather than budgeted

tx_span_us.description: radio. Microseconds from arming the last burst to the radio reporting it sent, which is the keyed time plus everything around it

tx_lost.description: radio. Bursts of ours that were armed and never completed: the dwell ran out, or the radio's transmit timeout did. Never a reception

range_refused.description: radio. Receptions core/traffic refused because the position they claimed was further away than this radio can hear (core/traffic/sanity.h). A rate that climbs is a receiver at the edge of its link budget or a decoder that is silently miscorrecting

dio1_armed.description: radio. The executor holds a rising-edge interrupt on the SX1262's DIO1 and sleeps on it between events. False on the host executor, which has no interrupt line, and on silicon when the GPIO driver refused the trigger: the executor then reads DIO1 every 200 us instead

dio1_edges.description: radio. DIO1 rising edges the interrupt handler saw since boot. Near rx and tx events combined on a healthy line; zero with dio1_armed true is a trigger that never fires

dio1_missed.description: radio. Events a status read found while DIO1 still read low: a TxDone read in the tail of a burst, the 4 ms safety poll, or the drain at a dwell's end. Rising with tx_ok means DIO1 trails TxDone, rising with rx_ok means it trails RxDone too

tracked.description: traffic. Aircraft currently in the table, after ageing out

alarm.description: traffic. The alarm level standing right now: 0 none, 1 info, 2 important, 3 urgent

fixes.description: gnss. Solutions the own-ship service has accepted since boot. Zero on a device whose receiver is wired but silent

valid.description: gnss: whether own-ship currently holds a valid fix. power: whether mv is the cell. False with no divider, on a reading outside 1800 to 4700 mV, and on the cable, where the divider reads the USB rail. The key is per group, so the two never appear in the same frame

baud.description: gnss. The rate we are ACTUALLY talking to the receiver at, which is the devicetree's rate until autobaud had to move. A receiver silently at another rate is a GNSS-less device that looks fitted

identified.description: gnss. The receiver answered the $PCAS06 handshake and named itself. False means an unidentified part, still configured, but a $PCAS dialect we cannot confirm

firmware.description: gnss. The receiver's own firmware banner, e.g. URANUS5,V5.1.0.0. Empty when it never introduced itself

reject.description: gnss. Why the last solution was not accepted as a fix (core/gnss/validity.h). A named cause, because every one of these has been a support case in one of the reference projects

rejected.description: gnss. Solutions refused since boot, one event per run of the same reason

resid_m.description: gnss. The extrapolation residual in metres: the model the transmitter applies, run over the interval that just elapsed and measured against the fix that closed it. ABSENT rather than zero when there is no pair of consecutive fixes to measure, because 0 m is what a perfect prediction reports

mv.description: power. The battery reading in millivolts, after the per-unit trim (settings.battery_offset_mv): the cell when power.valid, otherwise what the divider last read, 0 when the ADC gave nothing

percent.description: power. State of charge from the same reading, on the discharge curve. 0 unless power.valid

charging.description: power. The cable is in. No pin says when the charge ends, so a full cell on the cable still reads true

level.description: power. What core/power's cutoff rule made of the same samples: LOW about 12%, CRITICAL about 5%, FLAT the device taking itself down. '--' is Unknown: no believable reading yet

supply_warnings.description: power. Times the nRF52840's power-failure comparator (POFCON) has fired. Any at all on a healthy cell is a supply problem or a threshold set too high, and both are bench work

implausible.description: power. Readings the gauge refused: at or under 1800 mV, an unpopulated or unconnected divider rather than a flat cell, or over 4700 mV, which no 4.2 V cell reaches and a rail does. On the cable or off it. mv holds the last one while power.valid is false

die_temp_c.description: power. Die temperature in whole degrees Celsius, rounded away from zero. ABSENT rather than zero when no reading exists, because 0.0 C is a plausible hangar morning. Same key and same value as the status reply's
